blocks.x: Retrieval that cites or refuses: permission-aware RAG over your regulated document estate, where every answer carries its sources, its freshness and its permission lineage, and where the corpus contracts that make that possible are built first, not last.
Why corpus engineering decides the answer quality
blocks.sub: Canonical registry, dedup and ownership, the unglamorous work behind every good answer

blocks.x: Retrieval-augmented generation done properly is corpus engineering wearing a chat interface. The model is the easy ten percent; the ninety percent is deciding what counts as truth in your estate, who may see it, how fresh it must be, and how an answer proves where it came from.

The organizational parts bite harder than the technical ones: document estates duplicate across portals, the authoritative copy is rarely the most recent one, and permission models live in systems the search team has never been allowed to read. We build the contracts that fix that first, because every grounded answer downstream inherits their quality.
Everything below is build-order material: the failure modes we design against, the architecture that fixes them, and the gates a release clears before a user sees an answer.

nodes.detail: Semantic chunking with parent-document mapping; metadata enrichment (version, effective date, section) turns chunks into records.

nodes.label: Hybrid search
nodes.detail: BM25 + dense in RRF fusion; lexical catches identifiers, dense catches paraphrase — the fusion is measured, not faith-based.

nodes.label: Cross-encoder rerank
nodes.detail: Top-k reranked per query class; latency budget per class decides rerank depth — interactive and batch run different depths.

nodes.label: Scope filter
nodes.detail: Access control at retrieval time per query scope; the permissions model is the corpus model, enforced before generation sees anything.

nodes.label: Grounded generation
nodes.detail: Cited generation with refusal when evidence is absent; the persona never answers past its sources.

nodes.label: Groundedness harness
nodes.detail: Claim decomposition nightly: every sentence checked supported/unsupported/contradicted against retrieved evidence; scores published.

nodes.label: Citation store
nodes.detail: Answer citations with chunk lineage — the audit artifact that proves which document version answered the question.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read each contract. The scope filter sits before generation on purpose — permissions are enforced where the corpus is read, not where the answer is written.

Permission fidelity is the hard part
blocks.sub: ACL folding, corpus hygiene and the freshness contract, the three disciplines that decide enterprise RAG

blocks.x: Consumer RAG is a search problem; enterprise RAG is a permissions problem with search attached. The index must return only what the asker could have read, so ACLs fold into retrieval at query time, denied documents never enter candidate sets, and permission fidelity is tested with adversarial probes (privileged questions from unprivileged accounts) on every release, not just at launch. The canonical registry is the corpus-hygiene discipline: one URI per fact, superseded versions marked, ownership named, because duplicate and stale content is what makes retrieval confidently wrong.

The freshness contract closes the loop: every corpus carries a signed freshness SLA (how long a fact may serve before re-verification), the retrieval planner decomposes multi-hop questions rather than pretending one embedding finds them, and the eval suite is replayed on every index or prompt change. The operating console reads permission probes, freshness breaches and citation coverage as its headline numbers, those three decide whether the estate trusts the answers.

How do you stop the assistant from answering beyond a user’s permissions?

Permission fidelity is enforced at retrieval, not at the prompt: the index carries ACLs from the source systems, and a query only retrieves what the requesting user could have opened. Every answer traces to the documents it cited.
What does the assistant do when the corpus does not contain the answer?

It refuses. Groundedness gates force a refusal when retrieval cannot support an answer with citations, a measured refusal is the correct output, and refusal rates are a console metric, not a failure to hide.
How do you keep answer quality from degrading as documents change?

The eval suite is versioned and adversarial: each generation includes the queries that fooled the last one, and corpus changes re-run the suite before promotion. Quality is tracked per suite generation, which the chart shows.
Can this work with our existing document stores and ACLs?

Yes, the connector layer ingests from your stores with their ACLs intact; corpus engineering (dedup, staleness, canonical docs) is the first workstream because it decides answer quality before any model choice does.
What does our team own at handover?
The corpus pipeline, the eval suite, the console and the promotion gates. Your team can add a document family, re-run the suite and promote, we support the first two cycles, then step back.
